items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: I gather something from Rob Palmer, I've got something from Dutre, and even a little touch of Tea Gardens

ctx.x: Yeah. And she fell off the pen and dead and heart attack. So I attribute that to her grieving. She never forget him. And I did have a little hassle on her. This tune strutting with some barbecue. I understand she said it was his and she said it was hers. Well you know Lil was a very good musician. You see she graduated from some college down in Tennessee. I don't know if it was Fisk or what anyhow. She even went with her job. items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Rob Palmer and Sugar Johnny and Lil Hardin... were playing at Deluxe. It was a place right across from the Dreamling... So we began to make those places

ctx.x: So when was the first music that you were interested in? Did you start on the trombone or which instrument did you start on?

Well, my first instrument was trombone, but it wasn't my favorite instrument. I'd like to tell you, Bill, about how I come to study the trombone. While talking with Joe Oliver, it must have been somewhere around 1920, 1921, somewhere along there. He, I told Joe Oliver that I was going to take lessons on the trombone.
